factProposals.value: Viewing a patient's follow-up tasks and their history (ViewFollowUps) and creating, editing, completing and cancelling them (ManageFollowUps) are held by the Admin, Dentist, Hygienist, Assistant, Front desk and Office manager roles; Billing and Unassigned hold neither. The responsible person of a task must be an enabled account whose role can view follow-ups.

A follow-up is created for a patient with a title (1 to 120 characters, one line), an optional note (up to 500 characters), a due time (at most 366 days in the past and 3,660 in the future), a responsible person and an optional recall interval of 1 to 3,650 days, with a required Idempotency-Key header; an edit, completion or cancellation carries the row version the person saw, and a cancellation needs a written reason.

When a task is due its responsible person receives one in-app notification of kind followup.due in the notification center; it names the patient and the task through a source key and carries no title or note, and opening it goes to the patient's follow-ups.

Follow-up data is three tables: FollowUpTasks (status Open, Completed or Cancelled, closed with who and when, a unique recall link so a task makes at most one next task), an append-only FollowUpTaskEvents history (Created, Edited, Reassigned, DueChanged, Reminded, Completed, Cancelled, RecallCreated) and FollowUpReminderDeliveries (one per task, due time and channel).
A background hosted service runs the reminder pass every 60 seconds by default (FollowUps:ReminderPollSeconds; 0 turns it off) and logs one structured line per pass with its counts.

Reminders are delivered only inside the application, through the notification center. No email or text provider is connected; a reminder channel interface exists so one can be added later without changing the reminder pass.

If the responsible person is disabled or can no longer see follow-ups, the reminder goes to every enabled office manager instead and is recorded as a fallback; if nobody can be told, nothing is recorded and the next pass tries again.

Every follow-up action, including the system's reminder, is saved with its audit entry in one save (a failed audit write stores nothing); audit entries and reminders name identifiers only, never the title or note; the database refuses changes to the history and to a closed task.

decisions.statement: Found due reminders by scanning for open tasks that are due and have no recorded delivery for their current due time, instead of scheduling one job per task.
decisions.rationale: A missed run, a restart or an outage then only delays a reminder: the next pass sends everything owed, and a changed due time is a new reminder because the delivery is unique per task, due time and channel.

decisions.statement: Made a create idempotent by deriving the task id from the person and the Idempotency-Key, and made completion and cancellation idempotent by the task's state rather than by a key.
decisions.rationale: A repeat then meets the same primary key or the same final state and cannot create a second task or a second recall, even under concurrent requests.

decisions.statement: Added two dedicated permissions, ViewFollowUps and ManageFollowUps, instead of reusing patient-record or note permissions.
decisions.rationale: No existing permission matched the roles that work follow-ups (note permissions exclude assistants and front desk; scheduling permissions exclude clinicians), and dedicated ones can be changed in the permission editor.

decisions.statement: Sent reminders through a small channel interface with only the in-app channel built, recording each channel's delivery separately.
decisions.rationale: Email reminders are expected later but no provider or address exists; a second channel can then be added without double-sending the first or being blocked by it.

limitations.statement: Reminders reach a person only if they open the notification center; there is no second channel yet and no escalation if a reminder is never read.
A channel cannot report a permanent failure and there is no dead-letter store; a channel that defers or throws is simply asked again on the next pass.
A task nobody can be told about is retried on every pass and only counted in the pass log; since a pass takes the oldest 50 owed tasks, more than 50 such tasks could delay reminders for newer ones.
A recall is due exactly the interval's number of days after completion; weekends, holidays and the practice's opening days are not considered.
The list of people a task can be assigned to shows colleagues' usernames to every role that can view follow-ups and holds at most 500 people.
